<description>
The mempool fee rate estimator can't always return an estimate:

i)   right after first startup (or after re-syncing through IBD) it hasn't tracked
     enough recent blocks yet;
ii)  the mempool is empty or too sparse to fill the requested block percentile,
     e.g. after a cold restart with persistence off or a missing/corrupt
     mempool.dat.
iii) recent blocks cover too little of the mempool (low coverage); and
iv)  the mempool is still loading.

Previously, case (ii) with a healthy mempool will returned the fee rate
floor (the higher of the minimum relay fee and the current mempool minimum fee).
This can be a significant underestimation, since the now-missing mempool may have
held much higher-feerate transactions. The remaining cases surfaced the mempool
error directly from the combined estimate.

This PR makes the combined estimate (`estimatesmartfee` with
`fee_rate_estimator=none`, the default) fall back to the block policy estimate
whenever the mempool estimator isn't ready, instead of returning the floor or
surfacing the error:

- The mempool estimator now returns an error instead of flooring an unfilled
  percentile, so an empty/sparse mempool is treated like any other not-ready
  state rather than potentially silently underestimating.
- The combined estimate starts from the block policy estimate and only lowers it
  with the mempool estimate when one is available. An error is returned only when
  the block policy estimate itself is unavailable.
- Calling `estimatesmartfee` with `fee_rate_estimator=mempool_policy` explicitly
  still returns the failure.

When the mempool fails to load at startup (persistence off, or a missing/corrupt
mempool.dat), init notifies the estimator, which clears its tracked mined-block
window. Otherwise the estimator would keep a window describing a mempool the node
no longer has; clearing it makes the estimator report insufficient data until the
window refills from the current tip, so the combined estimate falls back to block
policy meanwhile.

This is an alternative to #36095.
</description>

[2026-09-24] c:5811183128 comment by ismaelsadeeq (member):
Forced pushed 86ef5cc277...3f68d2cdc6 to address feedback by @stickies-v  and @davidgumberg

- I added a check that prevents the economical estimates from being lower than the estimates, we only return an estimate when both have non-empty estimates.
- I prevent logging that we clear the mined block stats when the vector is empty.
- Removed stale mention of warmup in commit message.
[2026-09-24] rc:4091891712 inline on src/policy/fees/mempool_estimator.cpp by ismaelsadeeq (member) (edited 2026-09-24):
Valid observation, we do want to return the floor in that case, but as it is now, we do not have a correct and final approach mechanism that differentiates whether we are indeed empty, have just connected, have lots of our mempool, on testnets etc. So a valid e2e fix can be pursued in a follow-up, given that it is very infrequent, this minimal fix is okay, I think.
[2026-09-24] c:5817784558 comment by willcl-ark (member):
I’m generally happy with the PR now.

One API naming question before 32.0: should we rename `fee_rate_estimator=none` to `auto`, as [suggested above](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36182#discussion_r3983953920)? I agree that `none` reads as though fee estimation is disabled, whereas it selects the default combined behavior.

I know it's not been introduced here, but this PR might be our best chance to fix the public name before 32.0 is released...

As we coerce all unknown values to `none`, anyone who has been testing and has `none` in a script/application already, would not see a breaking change, which makes it feel even more appealing to me.

It could also be it's own tiny "bugfix" PR perhaps, too.

Happy to ACK this with or without that change, but wanted to see what folks reviewing this thought.
[2026-09-24] rc:4096755419 inline on src/policy/fees/mempool_estimator.cpp by davidgumberg (member) (edited 2026-09-24):
Latest push fixed this, thanks @ismaelsadeeq.
[2026-09-24] rc:4096852515 inline on src/policy/fees/mempool_estimator.cpp by davidgumberg (member) (edited 2026-09-24):
I'm not sure I agree, I think it would be better to drop the last two commits entirely from this PR, since it only sometimes fixes a problem that likely no one will ever run into:

- Fee misestimation because a user starts their node after a day off and their mempool.dat happened to be healthy for 6 blocks in a row (I think this is the thing that's most unlikely) *and* they request a feerate at that time *and*  it happens that at that time their mempool is nearly empty [if not empty the mempool estimator will still return an estimate]

And creates a problem that all users will run into infrequently:

- Overestimating fees whenever the mempool is starved.
